definitions.explanation: A feeling of active ill will or opposition toward someone or something.

examples.japanese: {敵意|てきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じた→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。

examples.english: There was clear hostility in his eyes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{理由|りゆう}→理由：01102_riyuu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦なく→ない：01118_nai⟧{敵意|てきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{向|む}けられて→向ける：02306_mukeru⟧、⟦{困惑|こんわく}した→困惑する：17192_konwakusuru⟧。
examples.english: I was bewildered by the hostility directed at me for no reason.

notes:
{敵意|てきい} combines ⟦{敵|てき}→敵：03546_teki⟧ (enemy) + ⟦{意|い}→意：30489_i⟧ (intent/will), expressing active ill will or opposition directed at someone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {敵意|てきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}つ→持つ：00478_motsu⟧: to harbor hostility
- {敵意|てきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{向|む}ける→向ける：02306_mukeru⟧: to direct hostility at someone
- {敵意|てきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧: to sense hostility
- {敵意|てきい}{剥|む}き{出|だ}し: openly hostile (lit. hostility laid bare)
- {敵意|てきい}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{抱|いだ}く→抱く：02010_idaku⟧: to hold hostility

REGISTER:
A formal word found in news, literature, and diplomatic language. In everyday conversation, people would more likely say ⟦{嫌|きら}い→嫌い：02871_kirai⟧ (dislike) or {怒|おこ}り (anger).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{悪意|あくい}→悪意：19922_akui⟧: malice, ill will (broader, not necessarily about an enemy)
- ⟦{敵|てき}{対|たい}{心|しん}→敵対心：27168_tekitaishin⟧: hostility, antagonism (slightly more formal)
- ⟦{反感|はんかん}→反感：08675_hankan⟧: antipathy, dislike (less intense)
